_about: Common ports and protocols for the Reference page (#ports). Well-known assignments from the IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry, plus a few widely used defaults marked default: true (not IANA-assigned to that service). proto is TCP, UDP or TCP/UDP as the service is normally used. secure lists the ports of the encrypted version listed here. exposed: true means it should normally not be reachable from the internet. tests/ports.test.mjs checks the shape.

source.title: IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry

ports.name: FTP-DATA
ports.use: Carries the files in active-mode FTP. Sent unencrypted.

ports.name: FTP
ports.use: FTP logins and commands. Usernames and passwords are sent in clear text.

ports.name: SSH
ports.use: Encrypted remote command line and file transfer (SFTP, SCP).

ports.name: Telnet
ports.use: Old remote command line. Everything, including passwords, is sent in clear text.

ports.name: SMTP
ports.use: Mail servers sending email to each other. Can be upgraded to TLS with STARTTLS.

ports.name: TACACS+
ports.full: Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus
ports.use: Login, permission and logging checks for network devices (AAA).

ports.name: DNS
ports.use: Turns names into IP addresses. UDP for most lookups, TCP for large answers and zone transfers.

ports.name: DHCP
ports.use: The DHCP server listens here and hands out IP addresses.

ports.name: DHCP
ports.use: Devices receive their DHCP address offers here.

ports.name: TFTP
ports.use: Simple file transfer with no login, used to boot devices and load configs.

ports.name: HTTP
ports.use: Unencrypted web traffic.

ports.name: Kerberos
ports.use: Ticket-based logins, as used by Windows Active Directory.

ports.name: POP3
ports.use: Downloads email from a mailbox. Unencrypted unless upgraded with STARTTLS.

ports.name: RPCbind
ports.use: Tells Unix clients which port an RPC service such as NFS is on.

ports.name: NTP
ports.use: Keeps clocks in sync, which logs, certificates and Kerberos depend on.

ports.name: MS-RPC
ports.use: Windows remote procedure calls (management, DCOM).

ports.name: NetBIOS-NS
ports.use: Old Windows name lookups on a local network.

ports.name: NetBIOS-DGM
ports.use: Old Windows broadcast messages on a local network.

ports.name: NetBIOS-SSN
ports.use: Old Windows file and printer sharing (SMB over NetBIOS).

ports.name: IMAP
ports.use: Reads email while it stays on the server. Unencrypted unless upgraded with STARTTLS.

ports.name: SNMP
ports.use: Monitoring and managing network devices. v1 and v2c use plain-text community strings; v3 adds encryption.

ports.name: SNMP-Trap
ports.use: Devices send alerts (traps) to the monitoring server here.

ports.name: BGP
ports.use: Routers exchanging internet routes between networks.

ports.name: LDAP
ports.use: Directory lookups (users, groups), for example Active Directory.

ports.name: HTTPS
ports.use: Encrypted web traffic. HTTP/3 also uses UDP 443 (QUIC).

ports.name: SMB
ports.use: Windows file and printer sharing. A common ransomware and worm target.

ports.name: SMTPS
ports.use: Email apps sending mail through their provider, encrypted from the start.

ports.name: IKE
ports.use: Sets up IPsec VPN tunnels.

ports.name: Syslog
ports.use: Sends log messages to a log server. Unencrypted.

ports.name: RIP
ports.use: Simple routing protocol used inside small networks.

ports.name: Submission
ports.use: Email apps sending mail through their provider, upgraded to TLS with STARTTLS.

ports.name: LDAPS
ports.use: Encrypted directory lookups.

ports.name: DoT
ports.use: Encrypted DNS lookups.

ports.name: FTPS-DATA
ports.use: Carries the files in FTP over implicit TLS.

ports.name: FTPS
ports.use: Encrypted FTP logins and commands (implicit TLS).

ports.name: IMAPS
ports.use: Encrypted email reading.

ports.name: POP3S
ports.use: Encrypted email download.

ports.name: OpenVPN
ports.use: OpenVPN tunnels (can also run over TCP).

ports.name: MS-SQL
ports.use: Microsoft SQL Server database connections.

ports.name: Oracle
ports.use: Oracle database connections.

ports.name: L2TP
ports.use: VPN tunnels, normally inside IPsec for encryption.

ports.name: PPTP
ports.use: Old VPN protocol with weak encryption; replace it.

ports.name: RADIUS
ports.use: Login checks for Wi-Fi (802.1X), VPN and network devices.

ports.name: RADIUS-Acct
ports.use: Records who connected and for how long.

ports.name: SSDP
ports.use: Devices announcing themselves on a local network. Abused for DDoS amplification.

ports.name: NFS
ports.use: Unix and Linux file sharing.

ports.name: Docker
ports.use: Controls Docker with no encryption or login; open to the internet means full control of the host.

ports.name: Docker-TLS
ports.use: Controls Docker over TLS with client certificates.

ports.name: GC
ports.use: Forest-wide directory searches in Active Directory.

ports.name: GC-TLS
ports.full: Active Directory Global Catalog over TLS
ports.use: Encrypted forest-wide directory searches.

ports.name: MySQL
ports.use: MySQL and MariaDB database connections.

ports.name: RDP
ports.use: Windows Remote Desktop. A top ransomware entry point when open to the internet.

ports.name: IPsec-NAT-T
ports.use: IPsec VPN traffic when a router doing NAT sits in the way.

ports.name: SIP
ports.use: Sets up VoIP phone calls. Unencrypted.

ports.name: SIPS
ports.use: Encrypted VoIP call setup.

ports.name: mDNS
ports.use: Finds printers and devices on a local network without a DNS server (Bonjour).

ports.name: PostgreSQL
ports.use: PostgreSQL database connections.

ports.name: VNC
ports.use: Remote screen sharing. Often weakly protected.

ports.name: WinRM
ports.use: PowerShell remoting and Windows management.

ports.name: WinRM-HTTPS
ports.use: PowerShell remoting over TLS.

ports.name: Redis
ports.use: Redis in-memory database. Often runs with no password.

ports.name: Kubernetes API
ports.use: Controls a Kubernetes cluster.

ports.name: Syslog-TLS
ports.use: Encrypted log messages to a log server.

ports.name: HTTP-Alt
ports.use: Common second web port for proxies, admin pages and test servers.

ports.name: Elasticsearch
ports.use: Elasticsearch search and data API. A frequent source of leaked databases.

ports.name: MongoDB
ports.use: MongoDB database connections. A frequent source of leaked databases.

ports.name: WireGuard
ports.use: WireGuard VPN tunnels.
